messages:
jon.p: Heads-up - got customer report: bulk SCIM failures after an OIDC client rotation. Provisioner returning 403 from KMS decrypts.
rita.sec: Any error snippets?
jon.p: From provisioner logs: `ERROR KMSDecryptFailed user=svc_scim_x err=AccessDenied: Caller not authorized to decrypt` and audit shows caller principal `oidc-client:old-client-id` while requests are coming from `svc_scim` in app logs.
kevin.ids: That suggests the OIDC rotation left an active token/service binding using old client_id that still tries to call KMS under a different IAM principal. KMS key policy probably grants decrypt to the new client only, old one lost permission.
jon.p: We rotated client_id and updated authz service but didn't cascade the change to the SCIM service's token exchange mapping. So some queued jobs were retried with the old client binding.
sre-oncall: Which tenants affected? Any PII in logs?
jon.p: Affected tenants: rivet-io, azura-net, four small customers. Minimal PII; we redacted emails in logs.
rita.sec: Immediate mitigation: 1) re-grant decrypt in KMS key policy to the old client_id for a short window, OR 2) revoke old client tokens and force a new token exchange, OR 3) pause SCIM retry queue while we reconcile. Risk tradeoffs?
kevin.ids: Re-grant is fastest to stop pages but expands blast radius. Safer: pause retry queue + rotate tokens for any long-lived worker that still uses old binding. We can do a narrow re-grant scoped to specific key aliases and set an expiry policy (1 hour).
jon.p: Can we quickly detect which worker instances are still using old binding?
audit-bot: Query suggestion: `SELECT instance_id, last_token_iss FROM auth_token_audit WHERE token_iss='old-client-id' AND last_seen > now() - interval '1 hour';`
jon.p: Running... returns 7 instances, mostly in a single region pool.
sre-oncall: I'll cordon those hosts and restart the scim service to force re-exchange. Meanwhile set a 1h temporary policy allowing old-client-id decrypt on the relevant envelope aliases.
kms-bot: Applied temp key-policy: grant decrypt to principal `arn:aws:iam::acct:oidc-provider/old-client-id` on aliases: env/rivet-*,env/azura-* with expiry=2026-03-24T15:45:00Z.
rita.sec: Good. Also ensure we emit an audit event for this policy change and link to the incident ticket.
audit-bot: Audit event recorded: audit_id=aud-7722 actor=kevin.ids action=kmspolicy.grant scope=oidc-temp expiry=1h ticket=ENGSEC-2220
kevin.ids: After restarts, provisioner retries succeeded for 6/7; one still failing because its token cache persisted old token for 45m. I'll flush token cache and trigger retry.
jon.p: Flushing cache worked. All retries now succeeded, no more KMS decrypt errors.
rita.sec: Root cause: partial rollout of OIDC client rotation without ensuring token-exchange bindings updated for long-lived workers + KMS key policy tightened to new principal. Contributing: missing checklist item to coordinate KMS policy changes with token exchange and retry queues.
kevin.ids: Remediations: - add preflight check that lists all live token issuers and verifies mappings before rotating client_id - update deploy checklist to include 'drain retry queue' or 'graceful token expiry' step - add CI contract test between authn (OIDC) and scim provisioner that simulates client rotations
rita.sec: Security actions: revoke any stale tokens, rotate any svc credentials that may have been exposed during the window, and publish customer-facing blurb if customers observed transient failures.
jon.p: I've filed ENGSEC-2220 for the runbook and ENGSEC-2221 for CI tests. Draft runbook link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/engsec/oidc-client-rotation-runbook (draft).
sre-oncall: I'll remove the temporary KMS grants at expiry and verify no further decrypt errors in 2h window. Also writing an alert rule that fires if KMS decrypt AccessDenied spikes after identity rotations.
audit-bot: Added watch rule and attached to ENGSEC-2220.
rita.sec: Postmortem notes: - root cause + checklist change - small blast radius due to narrow temp grant - required cross-team coordination (authn, scim, kms) - schedule a tabletop for client rotations next week.
jon.p: Thanks everyone, closing once policy TTL expires and metrics look clean. :thumbsup:
